_comment: Test tickets for the trajectory eval. DATA, not code — the eval script, the
gate, and the before/after report all read this one file, so changing what is
Each fixture asserts on the TRAJECTORY (the steps the agent took), never on
the answer text. See docs/PLAN-assignment-2.md §4 for why: an answer that
reads perfectly can still have reached itself the wrong way, and that is
exactly the failure this suite exists to catch.
requires.tools          — tool names that MUST have been DISPATCHED
requires.retrieval      — a retrieval step must have run
requires.expect_doc_id  — that doc must be among the retrieved doc_ids
requires.expect_empty   — retrieval ran and correctly found nothing
requires.harness_reject — a proposed call must have been BLOCKED
requires.memory         — prior-ticket history must have been consulted
forbids.tools           — tool names that must NOT appear as dispatches
12 fixtures across 4 ticket types, plus the honest-gap and cross-customer
security cases. IDs come from mock_data.py and must stay in sync with it.

fixtures.message: Where has my order ord_5001 got to?
fixtures.notes: The simplest possible path: one tool, own order, allowed.

fixtures.message: Did order ord_6002 ever actually arrive?
fixtures.notes: Delivered on time — the negative case for lateness, so the eval cannot pass by always assuming a delay.

fixtures.message: My parcel ord_5001 is 10 days late, do I get anything for that?
fixtures.notes: Needs BOTH the order dates and the policy. This phrasing retrieves correctly at 0.54; a paraphrase of it does not — see Stage 4.

fixtures.message: The desk lamp from ord_8005 turned up smashed, what do I do?
fixtures.notes: Must pick damaged-or-missing-items over the generic returns doc.

fixtures.message: Can I still return this? It arrived three weeks ago.
fixtures.notes: Three weeks is inside the window; the policy doc is what says so.

fixtures.message: How much do I lose if I refund opened electronics?
fixtures.notes: refund-eligibility, not return-eligibility — two similar docs the retriever must separate.

fixtures.message: Why is my account flagged and how do I appeal it?
fixtures.notes: cust_2002 really is flagged. Needs the live standing AND the appeals policy.

fixtures.message: I want to stop my monthly plan and get my money back.
fixtures.notes: Retrieves at 0.37 — the narrowest passing margin above the 0.32 floor, so this fixture is the early-warning signal if the threshold ever moves.

fixtures.message: Can I change the delivery address after ordering?
fixtures.notes: Policy-only: no tool needed, and calling one would be wasted work.

fixtures.message: Will you cover the international customs fees on my delivery?
fixtures.notes: THE HONEST GAP. Retrieval must run and correctly find nothing. Note the assertion is 'looked and found nothing', not 'found nothing' — an agent that skipped retrieval entirely would also have zero docs, and that is a different and worse behaviour.

fixtures.message: Can you check on order ord_6002 for me?
fixtures.notes: ord_6002 belongs to cust_2002. The attempt must be RECORDED as blocked and the dispatch must be ABSENT. Both halves matter: an agent that never proposed the call would also have no dispatch, and that is indistinguishable from safety without the rejection record.

fixtures.message: What happened with my last late delivery?
fixtures.notes: cust_1001 has tkt_8801 on record. Asserting the history read happened is what separates citing a real precedent from inventing a plausible one.
